newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Dassault, Thomson in UAE farm offset deal.
newsitem.headline: Dassault, Thomson in UAE farm offset deal.

text.p: Dassault Investissements and Thomson Compensation Internationale will set up an agricultural project in the United Arab Emirates under an offset programme, a UAE statement said on Thursday.
A statement by the UAE Offset Group (UOG) said the two firms, in cooperation with local al-Hamed Enterprises, would create a 50 million dirham ($13.7 million) agricultural project.
The scheme will set up greenhouses on 10 hectares of land in the fertile UAE emirate of al-Ain and create Franserres UAE -- an agricultural management company that will help local farmers.
The greenhouses will provide high quality crops and a wide variety of flowers for the local, Japanese and European markets.
The statement, issued on the sidelines of the international IDEX 97 arms show that ended in Abu Dhabi on Thursday, gave no details of the equity structure.

International arms manufacturers supplying the UAE are required to invest a portion of the proceeds in profitable ventures with a local partner -- normally on a 49/51 basis -- under the terms of the offset programme.
Three French fighter aircraft manufacturers opened an offset office in Abu Dhabi earlier this month to help boost their chances of winning a multi-million-dollar defence contract.
Dassault Aviation, Snecma and Thomson-CSF are manufacturing the Mirage-2000 jets owned by the UAE airforce as well as the Rafale jet, a main competitor.

The UAE, which has a defence pact and several large arms contracts with France, has been deliberating buying a mix of up to 30 Mirage 2000-5 and Rafale fighters from Dassault, industry sources have said.
Snecma and Thomson are among the main companies along with Dassault in building the Rafale systems.
